We want to understand what you meant by "something about the way the options were presented felt a bit mixed up to me", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The two large action areas near the bottom, “Continue Shopping” and “Place Order,” appear stacked close together, making it unclear which one is meant to be the main checkout action.  
B) The “Continue Shopping” option appears more visually prominent than “Place Order,” even though the screen is labelled as “Secure Checkout.”  
C) The payment details section sits above both options, but there is no clear separation or label explaining how the two bottom options relate to completing checkout versus leaving checkout.  
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
turns.a: If I had to pick... probably A? I think. Though I'm not sure that's exactly it — it might be closer to another option, depending on how you're defining it. It's more of a general feeling than a specific thing. Other people might not even notice.

turns.q: What kind of ordering or checkout situation would bring you to a layout where “Continue Shopping” and “Place Order” are shown together near the bottom?
turns.a: I'm not sure I have one specific moment in mind. It's more of a... recurring thing, I suppose. When the team needs to process something quickly and there's not much time for figuring out the interface. Though I'm not sure that's specific enough.

turns.q: When you noticed “Continue Shopping” and “Place Order” stacked near the bottom, what were you trying to understand or confirm about which checkout action was primary?
turns.a: I suppose just... complete the transaction. Confirm the order. I don't usually think of it as a 'job' — it's more like the last step in something larger. Getting it over the line without any detours.

turns.q: For the “Continue Shopping” and “Place Order” areas near the bottom, what would the layout need to show so the main checkout action feels immediately clear?
turns.a: I suppose just... make it clearer which button is the main one? Though I'm sure there are reasons it's set up the way it is. It's not really my call to say how the layout should look.

turns.q: Looking at “Place Order” specifically, what about its visual appearance — fill, color, contrast, border, or text style — keeps it from standing out as the main checkout action?
turns.a: The 'Continue Shopping' button — it drew my eye more than I expected it to. It looked more like the primary action, but it's not. The actual primary action — 'Place Order' — was less visible somehow. I almost went to the wrong one before I caught myself.

turns.q: Between the two bottom actions, does “Place Order” look too hollow or outline-only, too muted in color, or too similar in contrast to “Continue Shopping” to read as the primary action?
turns.a: 'Continue Shopping' was styled as if it were the main action — more visual weight, more presence on the page than I'd expect for a button that takes you backward. 'Place Order' — the actual thing I needed to do — looked secondary by comparison. That's the barrier. The fix: downgrade 'Continue Shopping' to a ghost button or a text link, something that reads as optional. And give 'Place Order' a solid fill color with real contrast so it's unmistakably the primary action. If those two things were right — 'Continue Shopping' quiet, 'Place Order' prominent — I'd have known immediately which was the right one without any hesitation.
